This finding is from an adapter that is not in scope for FedRAMP (pf-pingid-idp-adapter-2.10.jar). The Ping team has removed this artifact from the images to get FedRAMP Authorized, it is available here: docker.corp.pingidentity.com:5300/pingfederate:10.3.1-redhat_ubi_ubi8_8.3-rl11-x86_64-edge
The vulnerable SocketServer and ServerSocketReceiver components are not called by the adapter, this is a false positive. Fixed in version 2.13 of the PingID integration kit
The pf-pingid-idp-adapter does not contain httpclient as a dependency. It exists in a pom file of another dependency, but there are no calls to any httpclient methods in the adapter code.

FALSE POSITIVE. The vulnerable UntypedObject Deserializer class is not used in any PingFederate adapter codebase. The jackson version in the adapter will be upgraded in a future release of this adapter.

FALSE POSITIVE. The pf-pingid-idp-adapter-2.12.jar does not contain the vulnerable common-io jar, the detection is based on a dependency pom.xml file which lists the commons-io package as a compile/testing dependency. This file will be removed in the next release of the PingID IDP Adapter to resolve scan false positives.

FALSE POSITIVE. Please upgrade to latest version of idp-adapter. The lastest version has been updated to include lastest non-vulnerable version of jackson-databind.

False Positive The pf-pingid-idp-adapter bundles hibernate-validator:6.1.0.Final transitively, but Hibernate Validator is not used anywhere in the adapter code. All “hibernate” references found relate to IDE-supplied JBoss DTD files, not application runtime. PingFederate and its adapters do not deploy Hibernate or EL constraint interpolation logic. Therefore, CVE-2025-35036 is not applicable to this component.

FALSE POSITIVE. PingFederate and it's integration kits do not serialize or deserialize JsonNode objects using ObjectOutputStream and ObjectInputStream anywhere. Therefore, this is a false positive and this vulnerability does not affect the product.
